questions.question: In the Build and Integrate domain, what is the purpose of the SDLC Component object?

options.text: To track software licenses and compliance
To identify individually developed parts of a business application like microservices and APIs
To manage user access to development environments
To store backup copies of source code

explanation.correct: The SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle) Component identifies individually developed parts of a monolithic business application, such as microservices, APIs, and other components that can be developed and released separately. This provides visibility into what's being built before it becomes a deployed service instance. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/csdm-build-integrate.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Software license tracking is handled by Software Asset Management (SAM), not SDLC Components.
User access management is handled through roles and groups, not SDLC Components.
Source code backup is a DevOps function. SDLC Components track the logical components being developed, not code storage.

source.excerpt: The SDLC component, that Software Development Lifecycle Component, which identifies again the individually developed objects that could be part of a monolithic business application... identifying the individual microservices, the APIs, et cetera, that can be developed and released.

questions.question: What role is required to view and edit the Identification and Reconciliation properties in ServiceNow?

options.text: cmdb_admin
admin
itil
cmdb_editor

explanation.correct: The admin role is required to view and edit the Identification and Reconciliation properties. This is explicitly stated in the ServiceNow documentation for IRE properties. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/properties-id-reconciliation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: cmdb_admin is not the role required for IRE properties. While it provides CMDB administrative capabilities, the documentation specifies the admin role.
The itil role provides access to ITSM modules but does not grant access to view or edit IRE system properties.
cmdb_editor is not a standard ServiceNow role. The admin role is explicitly required for IRE property configuration.

source.excerpt: These properties are available for Identification and Reconciliation. To view and edit these properties, the admin role is required.

questions.question: What is the default value of the glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates.threshold property?

explanation.correct: The default value of glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates.threshold is 5. This property sets the maximum number of CIs that can be in a set of duplicate CIs before the system stops processing them as duplicates. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/properties-id-reconciliation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 3 is not the default value. The threshold defaults to 5 duplicate CIs.
10 is not the default value. The threshold defaults to 5 duplicate CIs.
20 is the default value for glide.cache.size.service_cache (the service cache size in MB), not the duplicate threshold.

source.excerpt: Maximum number of CIs that can be in a set of duplicate CIs to allow identification to process the duplicate CIs according to the setting of glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates. glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates.threshold ... Default value: 5

questions.question: What is the default AWS key rotation period (in days) for the Service Graph Connector for AWS?

explanation.correct: The aws_rotate_keys_period connection property defaults to 90 days for the Service Graph Connector for AWS. This defines how frequently AWS access keys are rotated. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-sgc-aws-props.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 30 days is not the default rotation period. The default value is 90 days.
60 days is not the default rotation period. The default value is 90 days.
180 days is not the default rotation period. The default value is 90 days.

source.excerpt: aws_rotate_keys_period | Enter the AWS key rotation period (in days). - Type: integer - Default value: 90

questions.question: What happens when the glide.class.upgrade.enabled property is set to false during IRE identification and reconciliation?

options.text: IRE silently ignores the class upgrade and processes the remaining CI updates
IRE rejects the payload with the reclassification update and creates a reclassification task
IRE automatically downgrades the CI to the nearest parent class
IRE logs a warning and forces the class upgrade regardless of the setting

explanation.correct: When glide.class.upgrade.enabled is set to false, IRE rejects a payload (or a payload item in Enhanced IRE) with the respective reclassification update, and creates a reclassification task. This behavior is consistent across all three reclassification types (upgrade, downgrade, and switch). See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/properties-id-reconciliation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: IRE does not silently ignore the upgrade. It rejects the payload and creates a reclassification task for administrative review.
IRE does not automatically downgrade to a parent class. It rejects the reclassification update entirely and creates a task.
IRE does not force the upgrade when the property is set to false. It respects the property setting and rejects the reclassification.

source.excerpt: Allow class upgrade during IRE identification and reconciliation. glide.class.upgrade.enabled ... When false, IRE rejects a payload (or a payload item in Enhanced IRE) with the respective reclassification update, and creates a reclassification task.

questions.question: How does the glide.identification_engine.update_without_upgrade_enabled property interact with the glide.class.upgrade.enabled property when both are configured?

options.text: glide.class.upgrade.enabled always takes precedence over update_without_upgrade_enabled
Both properties must be set to true for class upgrades to be processed
glide.identification_engine.update_without_upgrade_enabled takes precedence over glide.class.upgrade.enabled
The properties are independent and do not interact with each other

explanation.correct: The glide.identification_engine.update_without_upgrade_enabled property takes precedence over the glide.class.upgrade.enabled property. When set to true, IRE processes the CI updates but does not process the CI upgrade reclassification update. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/properties-id-reconciliation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is the opposite of the documented behavior. The update_without_upgrade_enabled property explicitly takes precedence over glide.class.upgrade.enabled.
The properties do not both need to be true. The update_without_upgrade_enabled property overrides the behavior of glide.class.upgrade.enabled.
The properties are not independent. The documentation explicitly states that update_without_upgrade_enabled takes precedence over glide.class.upgrade.enabled.

source.excerpt: glide.identification_engine.update_without_upgrade_enabled | Enable IRE to process CI updates with upgrade reclassification updates. This property takes precedence over the glide.class.upgrade.enabled property.

questions.question: Which types of CI reclassification can be individually controlled through IRE properties during identification and reconciliation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Class upgrade
Class merge
Class downgrade
Class switch

explanation.correct: IRE provides individual property controls for three types of CI reclassification: class upgrade (glide.class.upgrade.enabled), class downgrade (glide.class.downgrade.enabled), and class switch (glide.class.switch.enabled). Each can be independently enabled or disabled. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/properties-id-reconciliation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Class merge is not a reclassification type controlled by IRE properties. The three supported reclassification types are upgrade, downgrade, and switch.

source.excerpt: Allow class upgrade during IRE identification and reconciliation. glide.class.upgrade.enabled ... Allow class downgrades during IRE identification and reconciliation. glide.class.downgrade.enabled ... Allow class switching during IRE identification and reconciliation. glide.class.switch.enabled

questions.question: An administrator discovers that 4 duplicate CIs exist for a single server in the CMDB. The glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates property is set to true and the threshold is at its default value. What will the IRE do when processing an incoming payload that matches these duplicates?

options.text: Matching fails and an error is logged for the duplicate CIs
A new CI is created instead of updating any of the duplicates
The oldest duplicate CI is picked as a match and updated, and the remaining duplicates have their duplicate_of field set to reference the main CI
All 4 duplicate CIs are merged into a single CI record

explanation.correct: Since the number of duplicates (4) is less than the default threshold of 5, and skip_duplicates is true, the oldest duplicate CI is picked as a match and gets updated. That oldest CI is designated as the main CI, and the remaining duplicate CIs have their duplicate_of field set as a reference to the main CI. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/properties-id-reconciliation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Matching only fails and logs an error when skip_duplicates is false, or when the number of duplicates exceeds the threshold. With 4 duplicates under the default threshold of 5, the system processes them normally.
The IRE does not create a new CI when duplicates are found within the threshold. It selects the oldest CI as the main CI and updates it.
IRE does not merge duplicate CIs into one record. It designates the oldest as the main CI and sets the duplicate_of field on the others.

source.excerpt: true: If the number of duplicate CIs is less than the threshold specified by glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates.threshold, then the oldest of the duplicate CIs is picked as a match and gets updated. That oldest CI is also designated as the main CI for that set of duplicate CIs. For the rest of the duplicate CIs, the duplicate_of field is set as a reference to the main CI.

questions.question: An organization wants to configure the Service Graph Connector for AWS to use an AWS Config aggregator for collecting resource data across multiple accounts. Which connection properties must be configured? (Select TWO)

options.text: config_aggregator_name and config_aggregator_region
aws_rotate_keys and aws_rotate_keys_period
config_aggregator_account
s3_bucket_name and s3_region

explanation.correct: To configure an AWS Config aggregator for the Service Graph Connector for AWS, you need to set config_aggregator_name (the name of the configuration aggregator), config_aggregator_account (the AWS account where the aggregator is configured), and config_aggregator_region (the AWS region of the aggregator). Options A and C together cover all three required aggregator properties. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-sgc-aws-props.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: aws_rotate_keys and aws_rotate_keys_period are related to AWS key rotation, not AWS Config aggregator configuration.
s3_bucket_name and s3_region are related to Amazon S3 bucket configuration for collecting EC2 instance details, not AWS Config aggregator setup.

source.excerpt: config_aggregator_name | Enter the name of the configuration aggregator. ... config_aggregator_account | Enter the AWS account where the configuration aggregator is configured. ... config_aggregator_region | Enter the AWS region in which the configuration aggregator is configured.

questions.question: What are the two primary functions that the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) performs to maintain data integrity in the CMDB?

options.text: Importing data from third-party sources and creating transform maps
Preventing duplicate CIs and reconciling CI attributes from authoritative data sources
Scheduling discovery patterns and managing discovery credentials
Generating CMDB health reports and validating CI relationship types

explanation.correct: IRE prevents duplicate CIs by uniquely identifying them using identification rules, and reconciles CI attributes by allowing only authoritative data sources to write to the CMDB. These are the two core functions that maintain CMDB data integrity. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/ire.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import sets and transform maps are separate CMDB data loading mechanisms. IRE processes data after it arrives, rather than handling the import mechanism itself.
Discovery patterns and credentials are managed by the Discovery application. IRE is invoked by Discovery to process the data it finds, but does not manage discovery scheduling or credentials.
CMDB Health and reporting are separate platform features. IRE focuses on identification and reconciliation of CI data during data ingestion, not on health scoring or report generation.

source.excerpt: IRE prevents duplicate CIs by uniquely identifying CIs. IRE reconciles CI attributes by allowing only authoritative data sources to write to CMDB.

questions.question: Which role is required for full access to create and update CI identification rules in ServiceNow?

options.text: itil
itil_admin (on top of itil)
admin
cmdb_editor

explanation.correct: The itil_admin role (on top of itil) is required for full access to CI identification rules. The itil role alone only provides read access. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCIIdentificationRule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The itil role only provides read access to CI identification rules, not the ability to create or update them.
While the admin role may have broad platform access, the documentation specifically calls out itil_admin (on top of itil) as the role required for full access to CI identification rules.
cmdb_editor is not the role specified for managing CI identification rules. The correct role is itil_admin on top of itil.

source.excerpt: Role required: itil has read access, itil_admin (on top of itil) has full access.

questions.question: Why does the IRE identification process use dependent relationships when identifying application CIs such as a Tomcat application running on a Windows Server?

options.text: To reduce the total number of identification rules that need to be configured in the system
To ensure the application CI is identified in the context of its host, preventing ambiguous matches across multiple servers
To allow the application CI to inherit the sys_id of the host server CI
To bypass reconciliation rules for dependent application CIs

explanation.correct: Dependent relationships force the identification process to first identify the host (e.g., Windows Server) and then identify the application (e.g., Tomcat) in the context of that host. This prevents ambiguous matches because the same application path could exist on multiple servers. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/ire.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dependent relationships do not reduce the number of identification rules. They add additional context to the identification process by requiring the host to be identified first.
Application CIs do not inherit the sys_id of their host. Each CI retains its own unique sys_id. The dependent relationship provides identification context, not sys_id inheritance.
Dependent relationships are part of the identification process, not reconciliation. They do not bypass any reconciliation rules.

source.excerpt: Relying on 'config file path' to uniquely identify the Tomcat CI, isn't sufficient because the Tomcat application can run on multiple machines with identical paths. The identification engine won't be able to choose a CI to update. Dependent relationships force the identification process to first identify the Windows Server host on which the Tomcat application is running, and only then, in the context of the host, to uniquely identify the Tomcat application itself.

questions.question: Which enhanced IRE API option is disabled by default when using the CreateOrUpdateCIEnhanced() API?

options.text: partial_payloads
partial_commits
deduplicate_payloads
generate_summary

explanation.correct: The generate_summary option is disabled by default. When enabled, IRE generates summaries in the output payload with processing details such as the number of updates per class. The other three options (partial_payloads, partial_commits, deduplicate_payloads) are all enabled by default. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/ire.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: partial_payloads is enabled by default. When enabled, IRE isolates items that cannot be uniquely identified and stores them as partial items for potential later processing.
partial_commits is enabled by default. It allows IRE to commit valid items in a payload even when other items contain errors.
deduplicate_payloads is enabled by default. It causes IRE to merge duplicate items within a payload into a single item for processing.

source.excerpt: Generate summary: IRE generates summaries in the output payload with processing details such as the number of updates per class. API option: generate_summary which is disabled by default.

questions.question: Which methods can IRE use to generate an identifier key for a payload item? (Select TWO)

options.text: A combination of source_name and source_native_key values from the sys_object_source_info object
The CI's sys_id value stored in the CMDB
Identification criterion attributes defined in the identification rule
The discovery_source and first_discovered timestamp combination

explanation.correct: IRE generates identifier keys based on either: (1) a combination of source_name and source_native_key values from the sys_object_source_info object, or (2) identification criterion attributes. These keys are then used to match partial and incoming payloads. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/ire.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The sys_id is an internal ServiceNow record identifier, not an IRE identifier key. IRE uses identifier keys to find or create CIs, but does not generate those keys from existing sys_id values.
discovery_source and first_discovered are CI timestamp attributes that IRE updates during processing. They are not used to generate identifier keys for payload items.

source.excerpt: An identifier key is based either on: Combination of the source_name and source_native_key values from the sys_object_source_info object. Identification criterion attributes.

questions.question: An administrator needs to create a CI identification rule that uses attributes from both the CI's own table and a related lookup table to uniquely identify the CI. Which identifier entry option should the administrator select?

options.text: Use attributes from main table
Use attributes from another table (Lookup table)
Use attributes from main and another table (Hybrid)
Use attributes from Related Entries

explanation.correct: The Hybrid identifier entry option allows selecting attributes from both the currently selected table (main table) and from another related lookup table. This is the correct choice when attributes from both tables are needed for unique identification. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCIIdentificationRule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The 'Use attributes from main table' option only lets you select attributes from the currently selected CI class table. It does not include attributes from a lookup table.
The 'Use attributes from another table (Lookup table)' option lets you select attributes from a related table other than the main table, but does not combine them with main table attributes.

Related Entries are a separate section in the identification rule used to define related tables that reference the CI. They are not an identifier entry type for combining main and lookup table attributes.

source.excerpt: Use attributes from main and another table (Hybrid): Lets you select attributes from both the currently selected table, and from another table (hybrid identifier entry).

questions.question: Where in ServiceNow do you navigate to create a CI identification rule?

options.text: All > Configuration > Identification Rules
All > CMDB > IRE Configuration
All > Configuration > CI Class Manager
All > Discovery > CI Identification

explanation.correct: To create a CI identification rule, navigate to All > Configuration > CI Class Manager, select the class from the Hierarchy view, expand Class Info, and select Identification Rule. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCIIdentificationRule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no 'Identification Rules' module under Configuration. CI identification rules are managed through the CI Class Manager.
There is no 'IRE Configuration' module under CMDB. The CI Class Manager under Configuration is the correct navigation path.
CI identification rules are not managed under the Discovery module. They are configured through the CI Class Manager at All > Configuration > CI Class Manager.

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Configuration > CI Class Manager. Select Hierarchy to show the CI Classes list and then select the class for which to create an identification rule. In the class navigation bar, expand Class Info and then select Identification Rule.

questions.question: An administrator is configuring identifier entries for a CI identification rule and needs to understand priority behavior. Which statements about identifier entry priority are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Identifier entries with lower priority numbers are given higher priority
Identifier entries with higher priority numbers are given higher priority
Identifier entries with identical priorities are applied in alphabetical order by name
Gaps can be kept between priority numbers so new entries can be inserted without modifying existing priority order

explanation.correct: Identifier entries are applied based on priority where lower numbers mean higher priority. ServiceNow recommends keeping gaps between priority numbers so that new entries can be assigned unused priority numbers without reordering existing entries. Entries with identical priorities are applied randomly, not in any deterministic order. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_CreateCIIdentificationRule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is the opposite of how priority works. Lower priority numbers are given higher priority, meaning a priority of 1 is processed before a priority of 10.
Identifier entries with identical priorities are applied randomly, not in alphabetical order. There is no deterministic ordering for entries with the same priority value.

source.excerpt: Priority of the identifier entry. Identifier entries are applied based on priority. Rules with lower priority numbers are given higher priority. Identifier entries of identical priorities are applied randomly. You can keep gaps between the priority numbers, so you can assign the unused priority numbers to new entries without modifying the existing priority order.

questions.question: In the Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace, which engine is used to map and transform data from Dynatrace data sources into ServiceNow CMDB CI class definitions?

options.text: Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)
Robust Transform Engine (RTE)
IntegrationHub ETL Engine
CMDB Transform Engine

explanation.correct: Data from the Dynatrace data sources is mapped and transformed into the ServiceNow CMDB Configuration Item (CI) class definitions using the Robust Transform Engine (RTE). The IRE is used separately to insert the transformed data into the CMDB. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-integration-dynatrace.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The IRE is used to insert data into the CMDB after transformation, not to perform the mapping and transformation itself.
IntegrationHub ETL is a different integration framework. The Dynatrace connector specifically uses the Robust Transform Engine (RTE) for data transformation.
CMDB Transform Engine is not a real ServiceNow component. The correct engine is the Robust Transform Engine (RTE).

source.excerpt: Data from the Dynatrace data sources is mapped and transformed into the ServiceNow CMDB Configuration Item (CI) class definitions using the Robust Transform Engine (RTE). Data is inserted into the ServiceNow CMDB using the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

questions.question: When the Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace ingests process data from the SGO-Dynatrace Processes data source, how does it determine which CMDB table to populate?

options.text: The data is mapped directly to the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table based on the staging table schema
Application Dependency Mapping (ADM) analyzes the imported data and uses Discovery Process Classifications to identify the appropriate table
An administrator must manually assign each process to a CMDB CI class using transform map field mappings
The Robust Transform Engine automatically classifies processes using the CI Class Manager

explanation.correct: The target table for process data is populated using Application Dependency Mapping (ADM). The ADM adapter analyzes the imported data and command-line arguments, then identifies the appropriate table based on the conditions included in Discovery Process Classifications list. The resulting table extends the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-integration-dynatrace.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data doesn't go directly into cmdb_ci_appl. ADM determines which specific table (extending cmdb_ci_appl) is appropriate based on Discovery Process Classifications.
The process classification is automatic through ADM, not a manual administrator task. ADM analyzes command-line arguments and imported data to classify processes.
CI Class Manager is not the mechanism used for process classification. ADM with Discovery Process Classifications handles this determination.

source.excerpt: The target table is populated using Application Dependency Mapping (ADM). The ADM adapter analyzes the imported data and command-line arguments, identifies the appropriate table based on the conditions included in Discovery Process Classifications list, and inserts the data into the table, which extends the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table.

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator is planning to upgrade the Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace to version 1.10.0. What prerequisite step must be completed before the upgrade?

options.text: Back up all Dynatrace staging tables and disable all scheduled data imports
Uninstall the Integration Commons for CMDB store app and reinstall after the upgrade
Disable the reconciliation rules for tables extending the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table
Create a new OAuth 2.0 connection alias in the SGC Central view

explanation.correct: Before upgrading the Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace to version 1.10.0 or later, you must disable the reconciliation rules for tables extending the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table to avoid issues with data reconciliation. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-integration-dynatrace.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: While backups are good practice, the specific documented prerequisite for this upgrade is disabling reconciliation rules for Application-extending tables.
Integration Commons for CMDB does not need to be uninstalled for the connector upgrade. The documented requirement is to disable specific reconciliation rules.
Creating a new connection alias is not a prerequisite for upgrading. The required step is disabling reconciliation rules for tables extending cmdb_ci_appl.

source.excerpt: Before upgrading the Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace to version 1.10.0 or later, disable the reconciliation rules for tables extending the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table.

questions.question: Which Robust Transform Engine (RTE) operation type combines the values from multiple input fields into a single string, with an optional joining string parameter?

options.text: Copy
Multiple Input Script
Concatenation
Replace

explanation.correct: The Concatenation RTE operation combines the values from input fields into a single string, joining them on the optional joining_string field. For example, inputs 'input_1', 'input_2', 'input_3' with joining_string ', ' produces 'input_1, input_2, input_3'. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/cmdb-integration-commons/cmdb-rte-operation-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Copy operation duplicates a source field value to one or more target fields. It does not combine multiple input fields into a single string.
Multiple Input Script runs a custom script with multiple inputs, but it is a general-purpose scripting operation, not specifically designed for string concatenation.
The Replace operation substitutes matching substrings within a single input string. It does not combine values from multiple input fields.

source.excerpt: Concatenation: Combines the values from input fields into a single string, joining them on the optional joining_string field.

questions.question: When using the RTE Convert to Boolean operation, which input value produces a result of `true`?

options.text: "yes"

explanation.correct: The RTE Convert to Boolean operation outputs true only when the input is 'true' or '1' (case insensitive). All other values, including '11', '0', and 'yes', return false. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/cmdb-integration-commons/cmdb-rte-operation-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The value '11' returns false. Only the exact value '1' is treated as true, not any nonzero number.
The value '0' returns false, as documented in the Convert to Boolean operation examples.
The value 'yes' returns false. Only 'true' and '1' are recognized as true values by this operation.

source.excerpt: Output is true when input is true or 1, otherwise output is false. (case insensitive)

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are valid Robust Transform Engine (RTE) operation types provided by the Integration Commons for CMDB app? (Select TWO)

options.text: Glide Lookup
JSON Parse
Extract First Numeric
Field Validator

explanation.correct: Glide Lookup performs a database lookup on a target table based on specified fields, and Extract First Numeric sets the target field as the first numeric value found in the source field. Both are documented RTE operation types in the Integration Commons for CMDB app. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/cmdb-integration-commons/cmdb-rte-operation-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: JSON Parse is not a documented RTE operation type in the Integration Commons for CMDB app. The available operations include Concatenation, Copy, Convert to Boolean, Convert to Date, Convert to Numeric, Glide Lookup, and others.
Field Validator is not a documented RTE operation type. Data validation is handled through different mechanisms in ServiceNow, not as an RTE operation.

source.excerpt: The following operation types are available in the Integration Commons for CMDB app: Concatenation, Convert to Boolean, Convert to Date, Convert to Numeric, Copy, Extract First Numeric, Glide Lookup, Multiple Input Script, Multiple Input/Output Script, Regex Replace, Replace, Round Numeric, Set, Split, Trim, Upper Case, Upper Case Trim.

questions.question: An integration developer is using the RTE Copy operation to populate target fields from a source field. The `overwrite_existing_value` field has not been configured. If the target field already contains a value, what happens when the operation runs?

options.text: The target field value is replaced with the source field value
The operation throws an error because the overwrite behavior is not explicitly configured
The existing target field value is preserved and not overwritten
The source and target field values are concatenated together

explanation.correct: When the overwrite_existing_value field is not set to true, any non-empty target field value is preserved and not overwritten. The Copy operation only replaces target field values when overwrite_existing_value is explicitly set to true. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/cmdb-integration-commons/cmdb-rte-operation-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The target field is only replaced when overwrite_existing_value is explicitly set to true. Without this setting, existing values are preserved.
The operation does not throw an error. The overwrite_existing_value field is optional, and when not set, the default behavior is to preserve existing non-empty values.
The Copy operation does not concatenate values. It either replaces the target field (when overwrite is true) or preserves the existing value.

source.excerpt: overwrite_existing_value (optional, Boolean): If true, then the values of the target fields are replaced. Otherwise, any non-empty value isn't overwritten.

questions.question: Which TWO statements correctly describe the Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace? (Select TWO)

options.text: The recommended method for configuring a connection is through the SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace
The connector uses standard import sets and transform maps to process Dynatrace data into the CMDB
Data is inserted into the ServiceNow CMDB using the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)
The connector is provided and maintained by Dynatrace as a third-party integration

explanation.correct: SGC Central in the CMDB Workspace is the recommended method for configuring connector connections, as the guided setup method is being deprecated. Additionally, data is inserted into the CMDB using the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) after being transformed by the Robust Transform Engine (RTE). See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/cmdb-integration-dynatrace.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The connector uses the Robust Transform Engine (RTE) for data transformation, not standard import sets and transform maps. RTE provides more advanced ETL capabilities specific to CMDB integrations.

This connector is provided by ServiceNow, not Dynatrace. The documentation specifically notes: 'The Service Graph Connector for Observability - Dynatrace provided by ServiceNow is different from the Service Graph Connector for Dynatrace provided by Dynatrace.'

source.excerpt: Unless there are configuration issues, use the SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace to configure the connection for the connector, as the guided setup method is being deprecated. Data is inserted into the ServiceNow CMDB using the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

questions.question: In the Service Graph Connector for GCP, which engine is used to map and transform data from GCP data sources into ServiceNow CMDB CI class definitions?

options.text: Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)
Robust Transform Engine (RTE)
IntegrationHub ETL
CMDB Transform Engine

explanation.correct: The Robust Transform Engine (RTE) is used to map and transform data from GCP data sources into ServiceNow CMDB CI class definitions. The IRE is then used separately to insert the transformed data into the CMDB. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/sgc-cmdb-integration-gcp.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The IRE is used to insert data into the CMDB, not to transform the data from GCP sources into CI class definitions. The RTE handles the transformation step.
IntegrationHub ETL is a separate integration framework. The Service Graph Connector for GCP specifically uses the Robust Transform Engine (RTE) for data mapping and transformation.
There is no engine called 'CMDB Transform Engine' in ServiceNow. The correct engine for this purpose is the Robust Transform Engine (RTE).

source.excerpt: Data from the GCP data sources is mapped and transformed into the ServiceNow CMDB Configuration Item (CI) class definitions using the Robust Transform Engine (RTE). Data is inserted into the ServiceNow CMDB using the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

questions.question: Which of the following is a key feature of the Service Graph Connector for GCP?

options.text: Requires a dedicated MID Server for data collection
Requires agents installed on each GCP resource for scanning
No MID Server required for data ingestion
Supports only manual one-time data imports

explanation.correct: One of the key features of the Service Graph Connector for GCP is that no MID Server is required. The connector ingests data directly from GCP using REST APIs. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/sgc-cmdb-integration-gcp.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Service Graph Connector for GCP explicitly does not require a MID Server. This is listed as one of its key features.
A key feature of the SGC for GCP is that no agents or individual scanning is needed. Data is collected via GCP REST APIs.
The connector supports periodic data pulls. Once configured, you can set up the integration to periodically pull data from the GCP application.

source.excerpt: Key features: Get started quickly with a streamlined onboarding process. Use only the credentials you need. No MID Server required. Get end-to-end data coverage. No agents or individual scanning needed. Performant at scale.

questions.question: What is the recommended method for configuring a connection for the Service Graph Connector for GCP?

options.text: Use the guided setup available in the platform UI
Use the SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace
Configure directly via the REST API Explorer
Use the CMDB Integrations Dashboard to create the connection

explanation.correct: The SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace is the recommended method for configuring connections. ServiceNow states that the guided setup method is being deprecated, and unless there are configuration issues, SGC Central should be used. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/sgc-cmdb-integration-gcp.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The guided setup method is being deprecated. ServiceNow recommends using the SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace instead, unless there are specific configuration issues.
The REST API Explorer is not the recommended method for configuring SGC connections. The SGC Central view provides a purpose-built interface for managing the full connector lifecycle.
The CMDB Integrations Dashboard is used for monitoring integration status, processing results, and errors — not for creating or configuring connections.

source.excerpt: You can configure a connection for the connector by using the SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace. Important: Unless there are configuration issues, use the SGC Central view in the CMDB Workspace to configure the connection for the connector, as the guided setup method is being deprecated.

questions.question: After installing the latest version of the Service Graph Connector for GCP, an administrator notices that newly added data sources are not appearing in integration runs. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Reinstall the Service Graph Connector application from the ServiceNow Store
Synchronize the newly added data sources using the Advanced Setup section in the guided setup
Restart the MID Server to refresh the data source connections
Manually create new import sets and transform maps for each missing data source

explanation.correct: After upgrading the Service Graph Connector for GCP, newly added data sources must be synchronized using the Advanced Setup section in the guided setup. This is a required post-upgrade step documented by ServiceNow. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/service-graph-connectors/sgc-cmdb-integration-gcp.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reinstalling is unnecessary. The correct step is to synchronize the newly added data sources through the Advanced Setup in the guided setup.
The Service Graph Connector for GCP does not require a MID Server, so restarting one would have no effect on missing data sources.
Manually creating import sets and transform maps is not necessary. The connector manages these through the synchronization process in the Advanced Setup.

source.excerpt: After you've installed the latest version of the Service Graph Connector for GCP, you must synchronize the newly added data sources. Use the Advanced Setup section in the guided setup to synchronize data sources.

questions.question: When creating identification rules for non-CMDB tables in the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE), which type of identification rules are supported?

options.text: Both independent and dependent identification rules
Dependent identification rules only
Independent identification rules only
Reconciliation rules only

explanation.correct: For non-CMDB tables, only independent identification rules are supported. The Independent checkbox must be checked when creating an identification rule for a non-CMDB table. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-non-cmdb-id-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Non-CMDB tables do not support dependent identification rules. Only independent identification rules can be created for non-CMDB tables.
Dependent identification rules are not supported for non-CMDB tables. The opposite is true — only independent rules are supported.
Reconciliation rules are separate from identification rules. The question is about identification rules for non-CMDB tables, which only support independent rules.

source.excerpt: For non-CMDB tables, only independent identification rules are supported.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid types of identifier entries that can be configured when creating identification rules in ServiceNow? (Select TWO)

options.text: Regular identifier entry — selects criterion attributes from the associated identifier table
Dependent identifier entry — links the entry to a parent table's identification rules
Lookup identifier entry — selects criterion attributes from a related table other than the current table
Reconciliation identifier entry — maps attributes to reconciliation rules for data priority

explanation.correct: Regular and Lookup identifier entries are two of the three valid types (along with Hybrid). A regular identifier entry selects criterion attributes from the associated identifier table. A lookup identifier entry selects criterion attributes from a related table (lookup table) other than the currently selected table. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-non-cmdb-id-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no 'Dependent identifier entry' type. The three valid types of identifier entries are Regular, Lookup, and Hybrid. Dependency is a property of identification rules, not identifier entries.
There is no 'Reconciliation identifier entry' type. Reconciliation rules are separate from identification rules and handle data priority when multiple sources update the same CI.

source.excerpt: When creating identifier entries, you can configure the Search on table and Criterion attributes fields on the Identifier Entry form to implement one of the following options: Regular identifier entry — Lets you select attributes from the associated identifier table. Lookup identifier entry — Lets you select attributes from any related table (Lookup table), other than the currently selected table. Hybrid identifier entry — Lets you select attributes from both the currently main selected table, and from another table (Lookup table).

questions.question: How does the Priority field on an identifier entry affect processing within an identification rule?

options.text: Higher priority numbers are given higher priority, and entries with the same number are processed alphabetically
Lower priority numbers are given higher priority, and entries with identical priorities are applied randomly
Priority determines the order of reconciliation, not identification
All identifier entries are evaluated simultaneously regardless of priority values

explanation.correct: In ServiceNow identification rules, identifier entries with lower priority numbers are given higher priority (processed first). When identifier entries have identical priority values, they are applied randomly. ServiceNow recommends keeping gaps between priority numbers to allow inserting new entries without modifying existing priority order. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-non-cmdb-id-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is incorrect. Lower priority numbers receive higher priority, not higher numbers. Also, entries with the same priority are applied randomly, not alphabetically.
The Priority field on identifier entries applies to the identification process, not reconciliation. Reconciliation rules have their own separate priority mechanism.
Identifier entries are not evaluated simultaneously. They are evaluated based on their priority value, with lower numbers processed first.

source.excerpt: Priority: Priority of applying the identifier entry. Rules with lower priority numbers are given higher priority. Identifier entries of identical priorities are applied randomly. You can keep gaps between the priority numbers, so you can assign the unused priority numbers to new entries without modifying the existing priority order.

questions.question: An administrator needs to create a new identification rule for a supported non-CMDB table. Which of the following are required steps when configuring the Identifier form? (Select TWO)

options.text: Set the 'Applies to' field to the supported non-CMDB table
Check the 'Independent' checkbox to indicate the identifier can identify records independently
Select the 'Allow fallback to parent's rules' option to enable dependent rule behavior
Configure a reconciliation rule before creating the identification rule

explanation.correct: When creating an identification rule for a non-CMDB table, the administrator must set the 'Applies to' field to a supported non-CMDB table and check the 'Independent' checkbox. Non-CMDB tables only support independent identification rules, so the Independent checkbox is mandatory. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/create-non-cmdb-id-rule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 'Allow fallback to parent's rules' applies only to dependent identification rules. Since non-CMDB tables only support independent identification rules, this option is not applicable.
There is no requirement to configure a reconciliation rule before creating an identification rule. Identification and reconciliation rules are configured separately.

source.excerpt: Fill out the Identifier form: Name — Name of CI identifier. Applies to — Supported non-CMDB table. Independent — Must be checked to indicate that the identifier can identify a record independently of other records.
